findings.claim_broken: R2 'previous checkout, the backed-up env/unit/Caddy files, previous gateway' restores service. It does not: the backup rollback.sh restores was taken at step 8, AFTER step 5 (30-pause) made the maintenance site the active /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, so rollback.sh restores the maintenance Caddyfile and reloads Caddy onto it. After R2 the public endpoint answers 503 for every request and no runbook step says to run `drain.sh resume`. The `pre-$RELEASE.Caddyfile` that 30-pause saves is consumed by nothing.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with the suite's own Host harness (scratch test test_review__r2_revert_puts_the_edge_back_into_maintenance): monolith host -> edge_install + `drain.sh pause` -> `install.sh` pilot (backup taken) -> `rollback.sh <backup> ROLLBACK_TO_UNMETERED=no-pilot-request-was-accepted` exit 0, env file == monolith bytes, then `ACTIVE SITE AFTER R2 == maintenance`, `LAST EVENT: docker exec caddy caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile`. By reading: install.sh backs up etc/caddy/Caddyfile when present (line ~50), rollback.sh `tar -xpf` + `caddy reload` (lines 36-49). Fail-closed (503), but a documented revert that leaves the endpoint down is a real OPS-RECOVER defect.
findings.minimal_fix: Append `"$d/drain.sh" resume` as the last line of 90-revert.sh (after `systemctl restart marlin2b-vllm`; with the restored no-mode env it starts the dev units, waits /health and puts the release's normal site back), and say so in README R2. Delete the unused `pre-$RELEASE.Caddyfile` save in 30-pause.sh or make the revert use it.

findings.claim_broken: 'Every pending file and its history row are applied in one transaction; a failure anywhere rolls all of them back.' A migration file that contains its own `commit;` ends the transaction mid-plan; everything before it (earlier files + their history rows + the first half of that file) is committed, the later failure rolls back only the tail, the message still prints 'every pending migration was rolled back', and the next apply is stuck (DuplicateTable). D's nine files contain no transaction control today (grep: only a plpgsql `end;`), so the guarantee holds for the current plan but is not enforced.
findings.evidence: Drill D10b against pinned supabase/postgres: files 0010 `create table review_a` and 0011 `create table review_b; commit; insert … 'not-an-int'` -> `0011_review_b.sql failed (InvalidTextRepresentation); every pending migration was rolled back`, exit 3, but history tail `0009 0010`, review_a_absent=f, review_b_absent=f; re-apply -> `0011_review_b.sql failed (DuplicateTable)`, exit 3. D10c: `conn.info.transaction_status` is INTRANS after a plain file and IDLE after a file containing COMMIT.
findings.minimal_fix: After each `conn.execute(body.decode())`: `if conn.info.transaction_status != psycopg.pq.TransactionStatus.INTRANS: conn.rollback(); print(f'{version}_{name}.sql ended the transaction (COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside a migration)'); return FAILED` — plus a test_migrate case whose fake Conn flips a status attribute.

findings.claim_broken: '`plan` is read-only (`default_transaction_read_only`)'. psycopg opens the transaction before the first statement, and `SET default_transaction_read_only` only affects transactions started afterwards, so the plan's own transaction is not read-only; the mutant `plan_not_read_only` is killed by a string comparison (`conn.log[0] == …`), not by behaviour. Harmless today (plan issues only SELECTs) but the invariant as claimed is not delivered.
findings.evidence: Drill D11 with psycopg 3.3.6 against the pinned image: after `set default_transaction_read_only = on` in the same connection, `create table … ; commit` -> `WRITE SUCCEEDED`; with `set transaction_read_only = on` instead -> `ReadOnlySqlTransaction: cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction`.
findings.minimal_fix: Change the statement to `set transaction_read_only = on` (and the mutant/test string accordingly).

findings.claim_broken: 'rollback attestation cannot be bypassed by a flag typo' is true in the script (exact string compare) but has no killable test: the suite only tries the exact value and no value, so a regression to 'any non-empty value counts' survives.
findings.evidence: Own mutant `attestation_any_nonempty` (`[ "${ROLLBACK_TO_UNMETERED:-}" != "no-pilot-request-was-accepted" ]` -> `[ -z "${ROLLBACK_TO_UNMETERED:-}" ]`): `1 passed`, SURVIVED. Scratch test with values `no-pilot-request-accepted`, `yes`, `1`, mixed case, leading space: all exit 2 with no events on the unmutated script (behaviour correct).
findings.minimal_fix: Add one loop to the existing test asserting exit 2 and `host.events == []` for a typo value (e.g. `no-pilot-request-accepted`), and list the mutant.

findings.claim_broken: 'rollback to the unmetered runtime is refused when any pilot request was accepted' — the script checks no evidence at all; it checks only INFRX_MODE of the current env file plus the operator's typed string. Nothing on the host or in the DB (journal/ledger rows, gateway admissions) corroborates the statement.
findings.evidence: By reading: `current=$(env_mode …)`, `restored=$(tar -xOf …)`, then the string compare; no other read before `systemctl stop`. The usage spill (`USAGE_LOG`, legacy jsonl) is not a pilot admission record.
findings.minimal_fix: Accept as an operator-attested step (already recorded in the lock record per README R2) or, if corroboration is wanted, have the coordinator's R2 procedure read the hosted `infrx` journal/ledger counts before stating it; note the choice in infra/README.md §8.

findings.claim_broken: A migration whose statements cannot run inside a transaction block (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, ALTER SYSTEM) is not refused at `plan`; it fails mid-`apply` (exit 3, fully rolled back). Safe direction, but 'dry-runnable' does not tell the operator up front.
findings.evidence: Drill D9: `0010_review_cic.sql` (`create index concurrently …`): `plan` exit 0 listing it as pending with a digest; `apply` -> `0010_review_cic.sql failed (ActiveSqlTransaction); every pending migration was rolled back`, exit 3, history unchanged at 0009, index absent.
findings.minimal_fix: Optional: in `local_migrations`, refuse a body matching `(?i)\bconcurrently\b|^\s*(vacuum|alter system)\b` with a named reason; otherwise document exit 3 as the expected outcome.

findings.claim_broken: 'the hosted migrate step depends on I3B's rehearsal gate and cannot be skipped' — the dependency is prose only (G6 'recorded', step 6 parenthetical). Nothing mechanical prevents running step 8 without step 6: the in-image probe runs with `--network none` and cannot see hosted history, so a skipped migration surfaces only as the runtime failing readiness (exit 4 -> R2/R3). Also the README's step order is not covered by any test (own mutant moving the snapshot row after the pause survived), and step 6 names no revert row (R4 says hosted migrations are not reverted, implicitly).
findings.evidence: Own mutant `runbook_snapshot_after_pause` (README row '| 1 | coordinator | **Snapshot' -> '| 5b |'): `3 passed`, SURVIVED. test_rollout.py checks scripts, not the README.
findings.minimal_fix: Add to step 8's Record column 'step 6 apply output digest' and have 50-install.sh refuse when `MIGRATION_DIGEST` is not exported (one `: "${MIGRATION_DIGEST:?…}"` line), or state explicitly that the gate is procedural.

findings.claim_broken: 'versions = file prefixes' is the only thing compared: an applied history row whose `name` differs from the file's name passes silently (same as the Supabase CLI), so a renamed-but-same-version file is not detected on the applied side.
findings.evidence: Drill D5: `update … set name='something_else' where version='0002'` -> `plan` exit 0, `applied: 0001, 0002, …`. Hosted-shaped rows are otherwise refused: a timestamp version `20250901120000` -> exit 2 'versions this repository does not'; a gap row 0009 without 0008 -> exit 2 'a gap'.
findings.minimal_fix: None required (matches CLI semantics); optionally print applied rows as `version name` in `describe` so the reviewer sees the mismatch.

nonblocking.claim_broken: 'Every pending file and its history row are applied in one transaction; a failure anywhere rolls all of them back.' A migration file that contains its own `commit;` ends the transaction mid-plan; everything before it (earlier files + their history rows + the first half of that file) is committed, the later failure rolls back only the tail, the message still prints 'every pending migration was rolled back', and the next apply is stuck (DuplicateTable). D's nine files contain no transaction control today (grep: only a plpgsql `end;`), so the guarantee holds for the current plan but is not enforced.
nonblocking.evidence: Drill D10b against pinned supabase/postgres: files 0010 `create table review_a` and 0011 `create table review_b; commit; insert … 'not-an-int'` -> `0011_review_b.sql failed (InvalidTextRepresentation); every pending migration was rolled back`, exit 3, but history tail `0009 0010`, review_a_absent=f, review_b_absent=f; re-apply -> `0011_review_b.sql failed (DuplicateTable)`, exit 3. D10c: `conn.info.transaction_status` is INTRANS after a plain file and IDLE after a file containing COMMIT.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: After each `conn.execute(body.decode())`: `if conn.info.transaction_status != psycopg.pq.TransactionStatus.INTRANS: conn.rollback(); print(f'{version}_{name}.sql ended the transaction (COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside a migration)'); return FAILED` — plus a test_migrate case whose fake Conn flips a status attribute.

nonblocking.claim_broken: '`plan` is read-only (`default_transaction_read_only`)'. psycopg opens the transaction before the first statement, and `SET default_transaction_read_only` only affects transactions started afterwards, so the plan's own transaction is not read-only; the mutant `plan_not_read_only` is killed by a string comparison (`conn.log[0] == …`), not by behaviour. Harmless today (plan issues only SELECTs) but the invariant as claimed is not delivered.
nonblocking.evidence: Drill D11 with psycopg 3.3.6 against the pinned image: after `set default_transaction_read_only = on` in the same connection, `create table … ; commit` -> `WRITE SUCCEEDED`; with `set transaction_read_only = on` instead -> `ReadOnlySqlTransaction: cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction`.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Change the statement to `set transaction_read_only = on` (and the mutant/test string accordingly).

confirmed_blocking.claim_broken: 'The engine (127.0.0.1:8000) has no route here at all', 'Caddy is the only public listener', and the units' least-privilege claims (per-uid, read-only, cap-drop). The edge's control plane is Caddy's admin API on `localhost:2019`, unauthenticated, and every runtime container runs `--network host` - so the gateway and worker processes (uid 10001/10002, the ones that decode untrusted media) can replace the whole public edge config: a `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000` on the real :443/certificate makes the private engine public, and a `file_server` on `/data` (the `caddy_data` volume, readable by Caddy's in-container root) serves the TLS private keys. The Caddyfile comment 'stated so nobody widens it' is not pinned by any test (own mutant `admin_api_widened` survived), and infra/README.md records no such residual risk (grep '2019|admin' empty).
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Drill on the pinned caddy@sha256:14a9c0… with the real deploy/Caddyfile (INFRX_SITE=http://:8080, `--cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE --read-only`, in a `--network none` box; a sibling container `--network container:<box> --user 10001:10000`): before `GET /metrics` = `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`; `wget --post-data '{"apps":{"http":{"servers":{"srv0":{"listen":[":8080"],"routes":[{"handle":[{"handler":"static_response","body":"EDGE-REPLACED-BY-UID-10001 …","status_code":200}]}]}}}}}' http://127.0.0.1:2019/load` -> `load exit=0`; after: `GET /health` and `GET /metrics` both answer `EDGE-REPLACED-BY-UID-10001 (could be reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000 or file_server /data)`; `GET http://127.0.0.1:2019/config/` returns the live config. Pre-I2B the monolith gateway (a host process as ubuntu) could do the same, so the exposure is not new on the box, but I2B packages the containers as sandboxed while leaving their sandbox a loopback POST away from the public edge and the certificate store.
confirmed_blocking.minimal_fix: Move the admin endpoint off the shared network namespace: `admin unix//config/admin.sock` in both Caddyfiles (the `/config` volume is rw and private to the Caddy container's mount namespace); in lib.sh `caddy_site` and rollback.sh line 48 add `--address unix//config/admin.sock` to `caddy reload` (`caddy validate` needs no admin). Pin it: in `test_backend_deploy__the_edge_hides_operator_paths_and_sanitizes_health` assert both files contain `admin unix/` and that every `caddy reload` in deploy/*.sh carries `--address unix/`; add mutant `admin_api_widened` (`admin unix//config/admin.sock` -> `admin localhost:2019`). Keep verify-external's external :2019 check.

votes.reason: Confirmed by code and by a reproduced drill. Code (codex-i2b @ 5d68e50): deploy/Caddyfile:6 and Caddyfile.maintenance:6 set `admin localhost:2019` (Caddy's unauthenticated admin API); lib.sh:68 runs Caddy with `--network host`; marlin2b-gateway.service:23 and infrx-worker.service:17 run the gateway (uid 10001) and worker (uid 10002) with `--network host` too, so all share the host loopback. No test, mutant or README pins the admin address (`grep -rn '2019|admin' deploy tests` hits only the two Caddyfile lines). Drill in own namespace infrx-review-verify-0-0 (pinned caddy@sha256:14a9c0…, the real Caddyfile, INFRX_SITE=http://:8080, --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE --read-only, --network none; sibling busybox `--network container:` as --user 10001:10000): before, GET /metrics = 404 and GET 127.0.0.1:2019/config/ returned the live config; POST to 127.0.0.1:2019/load with a static_response config exited 0; after, GET /metrics and /health both returned `EDGE-REPLACED-BY-UID-10001`. So a compromised gateway/worker process can rewrite the public edge (e.g. reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000 or file_server /data with the TLS keys), which breaks the Caddyfile's own 'engine has no route here' and the units' 'Caddy is the only public listener' claims. The proposed fix is viable: with `admin unix//config/admin.sock` the config validates on the pinned image, :2019 refuses connections from the sibling uid, and `docker exec caddy caddy reload --config … --adapter caddyfile --address unix//config/admin.sock` succeeds (exit 0) with the /config volume mounted. Note: the exposure predates I2B on the box (Caddy on host net with the monolith gateway), but I2B is the lane that packages these processes as sandboxed and ships the Caddyfile, so the fix belongs here.

Confirmed, not refuted. All load-bearing facts check out in the I2B worktree (head 5d68e50): both Caddyfiles declare `admin localhost:2019` (Caddy's default, unauthenticated); lib.sh:68 runs Caddy with `--network host`; marlin2b-gateway.service:23 (uid 10001) and infrx-worker.service:17 (uid 10002) — the processes that decode untrusted media — also run `--network host`, sharing the same host loopback; edge_install starts Caddy with no `--user` (so root in-container) and mounts `-v caddy_data:/data`, the TLS key store. Caddy's admin `/load` replaces the running config (documented behavior). So a compromised gateway/worker can POST to 127.0.0.1:2019/load and replace the public :443 config — reverse_proxy to the private engine (127.0.0.1:8000) or file_server on /data to serve the TLS private keys — defeating the very least-privilege sandboxing I2B introduces and contradicting the units' 'loopback only - Caddy is the only public listener' claims. Nothing pins it: grep '2019|admin' over infra/README.md and deploy scripts finds no residual-risk note, no test isolates the admin socket, and verify-external.sh:28 only checks external reachability of 2019, which does not cover a container in the shared host netns. The proposed fix (admin over unix socket in the /config volume, which is not mounted into the runtime containers) is sound. The live drill was interrupted by a safety classifier, but it would only re-demonstrate documented Caddy admin-API behavior already established by the code.
